properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-28 in production: on flo2.io's 0.73.0 engine the nightly backup's container stop took about 1 s and the whole pause about 2 s, down from 10-12 s on 0.72.0
properties.source: the flo2-backup journal on the flo2 droplet, read from the dev_reflow2 hub session
properties.statement: FIRST PRODUCTION STOP OF A DRAINING SERVER. flo2.io's engine runs reflow2 0.73.0 as PID 1 in a container (--registry-root, 13 designs). The nightly backup at 04:12 UTC on 2026-09-28 logged "stopping reflow2" at 04:13:49, the archive written at 04:13:50 (11 MB), and "reflow2 restarted" at 04:13:51. On 0.72.0 the same stop took 12 s an hour earlier (03:16:43 to 03:16:55, the pre-upgrade backup), and 10-11 s on every nightly before it: the process had no SIGTERM handler, so Docker waited out its 10 s timeout and killed it. So the drain (#607, v0.73.0) removed about 10 s of the pause, which is most of what epoch:planned-backups-without-stopping-the-server set out to remove. What is NOT measured: whether any request was in flight during that stop (it was 04:13 UTC, quiet), so the grace path under load is still proven only by tests/a_server_drains_before_it_stops.rs.
